_note: Fertilizer dose tables in kg/acre for MEDIUM-fertility soil as [low, high] ranges; the tools use the midpoint. Two provenance classes, declared per crop in `provenance`: (1) 'kb-transcribed' — copied from data/knowledge_base/fertilizer_guide.md, which already states doses in kg/acre of product; (2) 'frg-derived' — taken from the crop's own table in BARC FRG-2018 (data/sources/FRG-2018.pdf), which states NUTRIENT kg/ha by soil-analysis class, then converted to product kg/acre using the official nutrient percentages in FRG-2018 Appendix-2 and 1 ha = 2.4711 acre. Each frg-derived crop records its source nutrient row in `frg_nutrient_recommendation_kg_per_ha` so every figure can be checked back to the page cited. Urea/TSP/DAP/MoP prices are REAL official Bangladesh government-fixed dealer prices (Ministry of Agriculture notification, April 2023). Gypsum, zinc, boron, cowdung prices are market estimates and flagged as such.

_derivation.why_medium: FRG-2018 publishes a separate dose row per soil-analysis class (Optimum / Medium / Low / Very low). We use the Medium row because fertilizer_guide.md — the source for the kb-transcribed crops — also states 'per acre for medium-fertility soil', so both provenance classes are on the same basis. A farmer with a real soil test should move up or down a class.

nutrient_composition_pct._source: FRG-2018 Appendix-2, Nutrient compositions of fertilizers (p196)

_derivation.caveat: FRG-2018 preface: 'Fertilizer recommendations suggested in this guide are not absolute values, rather indicative since they are based on soil test values of wider areas.'

T. Aman Rice.source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — T. Aman rice fertilizer dose

applications.note: apply full TSP, MoP and gypsum at final land preparation
15 DAT, after seedling establishment
30–35 DAT at active tillering
50–55 DAT at panicle initiation

irrigation.action: Transplant into puddled field with thin standing water
Mostly rainfed in Kharif-2 — irrigate only if the monsoon breaks for 10+ days and the field cracks
Drain 10–15 days before harvest to firm the field

Boro Rice.source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — Boro rice fertilizer dose

applications.note: all except urea as basal
20 DAT; keep 2–3 cm standing water
40 DAT at maximum tillering
60–65 DAT at panicle initiation

irrigation.action: Fully irrigated crop (~1000–1200 mm equivalent); maintain 2–3 cm standing water
No water stress from booting to grain fill
Drain before harvest

Maize (Kharif).source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — Maize fertilizer dose

applications.note: 1/3 urea + all others as basal
~25 DAS at knee-high with earthing-up
~45 DAS before tasseling; earth up after top-dressing to reduce lodging

irrigation.action: Sensitive to waterlogging — make drainage furrows every 4 rows in Kharif
Irrigate if a dry spell hits at tasseling–silking; stress here costs the most yield

Potato.source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — Potato fertilizer dose

applications.stage: Basal — in the ridge at planting
applications.note: 1/2 urea + everything else in the ridge; potato is potash-hungry
30–35 DAS with final earthing-up; excess urea delays tuberization and softens skin

irrigation.action: Light irrigation at stolon initiation
4–6 light irrigations total during bulking; avoid waterlogging
Stop 10 days pre-harvest to harden skins

Wheat.source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — Wheat fertilizer dose

applications.note: 2/3 urea + all others at sowing
immediately after the crown-root-initiation irrigation (20–25 DAS); top-dressing on dry soil wastes nitrogen

irrigation.action: Crown root initiation irrigation at 20–25 DAS — the most yield-critical water
Booting stage irrigation
Grain filling irrigation

Mustard.source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — Mustard fertilizer dose

applications.note: 1/2 urea + all others; gypsum's sulphur boosts oil %
18–22 DAS before flowering, ideally with a light irrigation

irrigation.action: One light irrigation with the urea top-dress if soil is dry
One light irrigation at siliqua fill if dry; mustard needs 0–2 irrigations total

Jute.source: BARC FRG-2018 via fertilizer_guide.md — Jute fertilizer dose

applications.note: 1/2 urea + others at final prep
30 DAS after thinning-weeding

irrigation.action: Pre-monsoon showers establish the crop; usually no irrigation after establishment
Needs clean slow water for retting 12–15 days at harvest

Brinjal.source: BARC FRG-2018 p102, BRINJAL (Solanum melongena), Medium soil class — data/sources/FRG-2018.pdf

applications.note: FRG: half the organic fertilizer plus all P, S, Zn and B as basal at final land preparation; the remaining half OF goes into the pits before planting seedlings
FRG: N and K in three equal splits at 20, 40 and 60 DAT, applied by ring method under moist soil
second of three equal N+K splits (40 DAT)
third of three equal N+K splits (60 DAT)

irrigation.action: Keep steady moisture after transplanting; brinjal tolerates winter and monsoon but needs drainage
Maintain even moisture across the long harvest window; waterlogging invites bacterial wilt

Tomato.source: BARC FRG-2018 p101, TOMATO (Winter), Medium soil class — data/sources/FRG-2018.pdf

applications.note: FRG: half the organic fertilizer plus all P, S, Zn and B as basal; remaining half OF in the pits before planting seedlings
FRG: N and K in two equal splits at 15 and 35 DAT, ring method under moist soil
second of two equal N+K splits (35 DAT)

irrigation.action: Steady moisture after transplanting; stake and space for airflow, never waterlog
Even moisture through fruit set — swings cause cracking and blossom-end rot

Onion.source: BARC FRG-2018 p109, ONION (Allium cepa), Medium soil class — data/sources/FRG-2018.pdf

applications.note: FRG: all OF, P, S, Zn and B plus HALF the N and K as basal at final land preparation
FRG: remaining N and K in two equal splits at 25 and 50 DAP for bulb production
second of the two post-basal splits (50 DAP)

irrigation.action: Shallow-rooted — irrigate lightly and often; it tolerates neither drought nor waterlogging
Light irrigation every 8–10 days through bulb growth
Stop watering to harden bulbs before harvest, then cure in shade

Garlic.source: BARC FRG-2018 p110, GARLIC (Allium sativum), Medium soil class — data/sources/FRG-2018.pdf

applications.note: FRG: all OF, P, S, Zn and B plus HALF the N and K as basal at final land preparation
FRG: remaining N and K at the time of first mulching, under moist soil, mixed in promptly

irrigation.action: Mulch with straw to hold moisture and suppress weeds
Light irrigation every 10–12 days during bulb growth
Stop watering to mature the bulbs before lifting

Chili.source: BARC FRG-2018 p112, CHILLI (Capsicum annuum), Medium soil class — data/sources/FRG-2018.pdf

applications.note: FRG: all OF, P, K, S, Zn and B plus HALF the N as basal — note chilli takes ALL the potash basal, unlike brinjal and tomato
FRG: remaining N in three equal splits at 25, 50 and 70 DAP under moist soil
second of three equal N splits (50 DAP)
third of three equal N splits (70 DAP)

irrigation.action: Plant on ridges or beds — chilli is very sensitive to waterlogging
Keep moisture even from flowering through fruiting; wet foliage in humid spells invites anthracnose

sandy.rule: split nitrogen into more, smaller doses (leaching loss) and add 25% extra MoP

clay.rule: full basal doses are safe; drainage matters more than dose

organic_rule.rule: where cowdung/compost 2 t/acre is used, cut urea and TSP by about 20%

weather_rules: Never top-dress urea within 48 hours before forecast heavy rain (>20 mm) — nitrogen washes away (30–40% loss).
Do not apply urea on drought-stressed dry soil — irrigate first, then apply.
Apply gypsum and zinc only as basal; they do not work as top-dressing.
